title: The front's cd into a worktree moves its session there
what: A Bash command of the coordinating session that starts with `cd <a linked worktree>` (alone or before ; or &&) is refused with the message to use `git -C <worktree>` or absolute paths, because Claude Code then moves the session's working folder into that worktree and keeps it there.
why: Seen 3 times on 25-26 Oct in session 3207dc59: a `cd` once locked the session into .worktrees/train-11; on 26 Oct `cd /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/tests-tmp; tail ...` and `cd /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/red-wave; sed ...` each moved the session's primary working folder into that worktree ("Primary working directory: ... (was /Users/amidman/relay)"). The user's rule already says "Use git -C <worktree>, not cd"; text alone did not stop it (principle 5: fact to code). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
failing_case: In the front session, `cd /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/x; ls` runs and the session's working folder becomes the worktree.
pass_cases: The same command from the main session is refused with the git -C message; `git -C /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/x status` and `ls /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/x` run; a subagent working inside its worktree is not refused.
where: plugins/core/hooks/guard-main.sh or the delegate routing guard: the PreToolUse check of the main session's Bash commands
